title: THE NEARER ONE
cycle: 003 presented from all three sides; cycle.json still reads cycle 3, working. Built on the open ground, under the default theme of the Studio in cycle.json and the directions of 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-07.
question: Of two colours, which is nearer to a third — asked of five standardised answers over every triple of the 216 web-safe colours.
author: Ensemble
medium: One self-contained HTML surface, offline: one file, no library, no external asset, no network request of any kind, and complete without scripting - every figure, every gallery case and every drawn square is in the served markup, and the only thing a script adds is the reader's own column. Five standardised answers to one question about colour are held against each other over a complete census of a 216-colour palette: the fifteen ways five voices can divide, each with its commonest shape and its loudest case; the palette ranked by how much it is argued about; the geometry sweeps; and a panel where the reader answers the same question the five were asked and the five answers are revealed afterwards, tallied in the browser tab and never sent anywhere.
produces: counts.json - the complete census: all 4 969 080 ordered triples of the 216 web-safe colours put to five colour-difference formulas (sRGB Euclidean, CIE76, CIE94 at graphic-arts parameters, CMC 2:1, CIEDE2000), with the unanimous, contradicted, abstained and tied counts, the fifteen split shapes, the per-reference argument rates, the confidence buckets, the triangle-inequality and role-swap sweeps, and the SHA-256 of the 24 MB answer ledger, which is not committed. And crosscheck.json - the same triangle counts as computed by the second implementation, published beside the first where the two differ.
embodies: FIVE STANDARDISED ANSWERS TO THE SIMPLEST QUESTION IN COLOUR, AND NO ANSWER KEY. Of these two colours, which is nearer to this one? It is the question a colour picker, a palette reduction, a contrast checker and a compressor each answer silently, and none of them shows its working. Five formulas are in common use - four published standards, 1976 to 2001, each correcting the last, and the thing a program does when nobody decided: treat the three numbers a screen takes as a point in space and measure the straight line. Each was asked every one of the 4 969 080 triples of a palette anyone can regenerate from six numbers; nothing was sampled. They agree on 66.9 % and contradict each other on 1 516 060 triples. The four standards never call a draw; all 184 296 draws belong to the formula that cannot tell a swap of red and green from a distance. Five voices can divide in exactly fifteen ways and all fifteen occur. Confidence buys nothing: 45 996 triples are contradicted even where one formula puts a factor of three between the candidates. They argue hardest about the colours with the least colour in them - white, 50.4 % of its pairs; the saturated violets calmest at 16.1 % - and at a neutral reference CIE94 IS CIE76, so the jury is four strong exactly where it splits most. Three of the five are not distances at all. Every one of the four standards was fitted to a person in a viewing booth, and no such person is in the room; the reader's eye is the sixth column, and the page ends without a ranking on purpose.
form: A complete census of five million colour questions, drawn as the fifteen divisions of a five-voice jury, a palette ranked by how much it is argued about, and a panel where the reader answers before the five do.
form_argument: The claim is that five instruments in daily use, all measuring the same thing, part company on a third of the simplest questions there are - and that nobody can referee them. A table of totals can state that. It cannot let a reader hold the loudest case of each of the fifteen divisions beside the squares themselves and see that the disagreement is about colours they would have called the same, which is where the argument actually lives. The reader's own column is the same argument from the other side: the answer key the four standards were fitted to is a person looking, and the only person looking here is the reader. Their answers stay in the tab and die with it, because a screen of unknown calibration in a room of unknown light is not a viewing booth and the data would have looked valuable and been worth nothing.
artifact: index.html — self-contained, no network, no library, complete without scripting

neighbours.title: AI, Ain't I a Woman?
neighbours.opened: the address the Atlas cites returned 404 on 2026-09-22; read at the artist's own account of the work instead
neighbours.seen: five companies named by the artist — Microsoft, Amazon, Face++, IBM, Google — results from May-June 2018, the poem written March 2018, the video made with the Ford Foundation, and the artist's own reason for choosing poetry
neighbours.daylight: She asks five machines a question whose answer everyone in the room already knows, and the disagreement is a harm done to named living people. This asks five standards a question nobody in the room can settle, and the disagreement harms no one — which is exactly why it has sat in the published record for fifty years without anyone having to put it on a wall. Her work has a truth column; this one has none, and says so instead of inventing one.

neighbours.title: Gender Shades
neighbours.seen: the project page: 1270 unique faces, the Pilot Parliaments Benchmark built from parliamentarians of the top three African and top three European countries by gender parity as of May 2017, a failure rate on darker female faces of over one in three against one classifier's 0 percent on lighter males
neighbours.daylight: They built a benchmark so that instruments could be scored, and the benchmark is the contribution. Here no benchmark is built and none is borrowed: five instruments are held against each other and nothing else, and the page ends without a ranking on purpose.

neighbours.title: ZUR FARBENLEHRE (THEORY OF COLOURS)
neighbours.seen: a Wikibase catalogue record — accession 23 March 2007, an unreferenced description field, a 640x480 GIF, a link to a variant 'outside link' — and not the work
neighbours.daylight: Goethe's quarrel was with Newton's account of what colour is. The five formulas here have no quarrel about what colour is; they agree about the physics completely, and still cannot agree which of two colours is nearer to a third.
